record.title: A preprint proposes context-conditioned control of multi-token decoding horizons
record.summary: A new preprint proposes choosing the number of draft tokens in multi-token speculative decoding from context-dependent acceptance forecasts and measured round costs. Its controller selects the horizon before drafting, uses exact-verifier feedback to update online, and is paired with a regret analysis. In five draft-target pairings over AIME 2025 and GSM8K, the authors report small, uneven gains over fixed horizons (up to 10%, with 8 of 10 settings matching or ahead). The larger up-to-4.1x figure is against plain decoding. The tests disable the KV-cache and use no fixed random seed; one AIME table row has an unexplained 3.7x adaptive/fixed throughput gap. These are credible but unconfirmed paper-reported results, not an established serving improvement.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The preprint introduces Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction (AMTP), a training-free controller that chooses the MTP draft horizon before each round using predicted acceptance hazards and estimated round costs, then updates from verification feedback. The authors state the exact verifier remains unchanged.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors derive a bound transferring online hazard-prediction error to throughput regret against the best horizon at each visited context, and give a sublinear-regret result for online gradient descent under their assumptions.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across five draft-target pairings and AIME 2025/GSM8K, the paper reports AMTP matches or exceeds a fixed horizon in 8 of 10 settings and claims throughput gains up to 10% versus fixed-window decoding; gains are not uniform and several rows show parity or regressions. Its up-to-4.1x figure compares speculative decoding against plain decoding, not the incremental effect of AMTP over fixed-window speculation.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Appendix D states runs disable the KV-cache, use no fixed random seed and process one sample at a time. Some benchmark conditions are capped or have uninformative task accuracy; the authors report throughput and acceptance only for base-model rows where accuracy is not meaningful.

claims.label: DISPUTED
claims.text: Appendix D.3 table 7 reports 28.2 tokens/s and 0.07 generation hours for adaptive Meta MTP 7B to Llama-2-13B AIME, versus 7.6 tokens/s and 0.54 hours for fixed k=4. The same appendix describes the same hardware group and evaluation regime; the paper provides no visible reconciliation for this large gap. The values are source-reported, not independently checked.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: No independent reproduction, fixed-seed variance estimate, production KV-cache evaluation, or verified author-linked code artifact is established by this activation.

evidence_gaps.description: The preprint refers to a released code lock file but the inspected paper/page and exact-title/identifier searches did not surface the author-controlled repository.
No independent, repeated-seed reproduction verifies the reported AMTP-versus-fixed-horizon gains.
The Llama-2-13B AIME row reports 28.2 tok/s adaptive vs 7.6 fixed and 0.07 vs 0.54 generation hours, a large unexplained discrepancy under the same stated hardware group.
All experiments disable the KV-cache, while serving cost and viable MTP horizon can change with cache use and production batching/concurrency.

brief.importance_rationale: If the proposed controller generalizes, it could make multi-token inference more efficient by choosing a horizon from context and verification feedback without retraining or changing the exact verifier. The reported benefit over fixed horizons is modest and uneven, so impact is meaningful but bounded.
limitations: All empirical outcomes are reported by the paper authors and remain unconfirmed here.
The reported tests disable the KV-cache and have no fixed random seed; deployment effects may differ.
The AMTP-versus-fixed comparison is mixed; some rows are at parity or regress, while the reported maximum improvement over fixed horizons is 10%.
One Llama-2-13B AIME table row has an unexplained 28.2 vs 7.6 tok/s adaptive/fixed difference and 0.07 vs 0.54 hours.
Theoretical guarantees have not been independently audited; they depend on the assumptions stated in the paper.
Exact-title/arXiv-ID searches did not surface the author-linked code artifact, but this bounded search does not prove no artifact exists.

Adaptive MTP and speculative-decoding horizon selection predate this paper; its narrower contribution is a training-free pre-draft controller with context-conditioned online hazard forecasts and the associated analysis.
brief.summary: A new preprint proposes choosing the number of draft tokens in multi-token speculative decoding from context-dependent acceptance forecasts and measured round costs. Its controller selects the horizon before drafting, uses exact-verifier feedback to update online, and is paired with a regret analysis. In five draft-target pairings over AIME 2025 and GSM8K, the authors report small, uneven gains over fixed horizons (up to 10%, with 8 of 10 settings matching or ahead). The larger up-to-4.1x figure is against plain decoding. The tests disable the KV-cache and use no fixed random seed; one AIME table row has an unexplained 3.7x adaptive/fixed throughput gap. These are credible but unconfirmed paper-reported results, not an established serving improvement.

technical.claimed_result: The paper reports five draft-target pairings across AIME 2025 and GSM8K. It says AMTP matches or outperforms fixed windows in 8/10 settings, with up to 10% throughput gain over fixed speculation, and reaches up to 4.1x versus plain decoding. Direct comparison tables show varied outcomes: Qwen3-4B self-speculation is 34.5 vs 34.0 tok/s on AIME and 38.3 vs 38.6 on GSM8K; Medusa Llama-3.1-8B is 25.3 vs 23.6 on AIME and 19.4 vs 20.0 on GSM8K. The Llama-2-13B AIME row reports 28.2 vs 7.6 tok/s without a visible explanation for the discrepancy.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected arXiv v1 contains the proposed mechanism, theorem statements and reported tables. the research desk did not independently verify the proofs, run the code, or reproduce the numerical results.
technical.mechanism: Before each draft, AMTP predicts position-wise conditional rejection hazards from pre-draft features, converts them to expected accepted-token counts, estimates total round costs, and picks the horizon with the highest predicted tokens per second. A randomized full-horizon exploration arm supplies feedback at positions short horizons would not reveal; inverse-probability weighting updates the predictor. The verification algorithm and target distribution are unchanged.
technical.regime: AIME 2025 and GSM8K with five pairs using Qwen3-4B MTP, Meta MTP 7B, Medusa Llama-3.1-8B and target models Llama-2-7B/13B and Qwen3-14B. The paper disables KV-cache for all runs, processes a single sample at a time, uses no fixed random seed, and reports capped Meta-MTP and Medusa conditions. Reported results concern a paper implementation, not production serving.
technical.reproducibility: The preprint provides a detailed method and setup and says package versions are pinned in a released code lock file, but an author-linked code repository was not surfaced by the exact-title/arXiv-ID searches or the page's displayed links. The benchmark is not bit-for-bit repeatable because no fixed random seed is used. No independent reproduction was found or attempted.
technical.strongest_baseline: The relevant baseline for AMTP's incremental effect is the same MTP/draft-target pair with a fixed window, not plain autoregressive decoding. Against fixed windows, measured outcomes are mixed and generally close; the abstract reports up to 10% improvement in eight of ten settings. The largest table gap is an unexplained Llama-2-13B AIME row (28.2 vs 7.6 tok/s), which requires artifact/log verification.

brief.title: A preprint proposes context-conditioned control of multi-token decoding horizons
brief.why_it_matters: Speculative decoding's efficiency depends on how many proposed tokens survive exact verification. A controller that adapts this horizon before drafting could reduce wasted inference work without retraining. The paper's formal framing is useful for inference research, but its measured improvement over already-speculative fixed-window decoding is modest and inconsistent; the reported tests omit KV-caching, and one result row is unexplained.
